concept.name: Cryptoasset
concept.definition: A type of private-sector digital asset that depends primarily on cryptography and distributed ledger technology (or similar technology) as part of its perceived or inherent value — the working definition used by the FSB and fellow standard-setting bodies. The category spans unbacked assets such as bitcoin as well as tokens used for platform access or in decentralized finance, and is distinguished from stablecoins by the absence of a stabilization mechanism.
concept.intuition: A cryptoasset is digital value secured by cryptography and recorded on a shared ledger rather than by an issuer's promise — its worth rests on what the network and its users make of it.
concept.mechanics: Cryptoassets are issued and transferred on distributed ledgers, with ownership controlled by private keys and transactions validated by the network's consensus mechanism. They trade on crypto-asset platforms around the clock; unbacked assets like bitcoin have no redemption claim, so price is set entirely by supply and demand.
concept.failure_modes: Prices are extremely volatile, and the market has repeatedly seen platform failures, custody losses, fraud, and contagion (the 2022 crypto-asset market collapse). Regulatory treatment is fragmented across jurisdictions, and interconnections with the wider financial system create channels for spillovers.
concept.misconceptions: That 'crypto' is one homogeneous asset class — the FSB framework distinguishes unbacked crypto-assets from stablecoins by function and risk. Also, holding a cryptoasset on a platform is not the same as holding the keys; platform balances are claims on an intermediary.
concept.example: Bitcoin is an unbacked cryptoasset: it transfers on its own blockchain between pseudonymous addresses, carries no issuer's redemption promise, and its dollar price floats freely.

citations.source: FSB: High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Crypto-asset Activities and Markets: Final report
